910.name: Elamite Civilization
910.description: The ancient civilization of Elam in southwestern Iran, one of the earliest urban cultures, its rivalry with Mesopotamian powers, and the magnificent ziggurats of Chogha Zanbil.

sub_clusters.name: Proto-Elamite and Old Elamite Periods
sub_clusters.description: The development of Proto-Elamite script at Susa, the Awan and Shimashki dynasties, and Elam's complex relationship with Sumerian and Akkadian Mesopotamia.

sub_clusters.name: Middle and Neo-Elamite Kingdoms
sub_clusters.description: The zenith of Elamite power under the Shutrukid dynasty, the construction of Chogha Zanbil, the sack of Babylon, Ashurbanipal's destruction of Susa, and the eventual absorption by the Achaemenids.
key_events: Construction of the Chogha Zanbil ziggurat, finest surviving example in the world (c. 1250 BC)
Ashurbanipal of Assyria destroys Susa and devastates Elam (646 BC)

910.name: Median and Achaemenid Empires
910.description: The rise of the Iranian Medes and the Achaemenid Persians, Cyrus the Great's creation of the first world empire, Darius' administrative genius, and the Greco-Persian Wars.

sub_clusters.name: Median Empire
sub_clusters.description: The unification of the Median tribes under Deioces, the alliance with Babylon to destroy Assyria, and the Median Empire as the first Iranian imperial state.
key_events: Medes and Babylonians sack Nineveh, ending the Assyrian Empire (612 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Cyrus the Great and Achaemenid Founding
sub_clusters.description: Cyrus the Great's conquest of Media, Lydia, and Babylon, the Cyrus Cylinder and religious tolerance, Cambyses' conquest of Egypt, and Darius I's reorganization into satrapies.
key_events: Cyrus the Great conquers Babylon and issues the Cyrus Cylinder (539 BC)
Darius I builds Persepolis and reorganizes the empire into 20 satrapies (c. 518 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Greco-Persian Wars and Decline
sub_clusters.description: The Persian invasions of Greece under Darius and Xerxes, the battles of Marathon, Thermopylae, and Salamis, and Alexander the Great's conquest and burning of Persepolis.
key_events: Battle of Thermopylae and Salamis (480 BC)
Alexander the Great defeats Darius III and burns Persepolis (330 BC)

910.name: Seleucid and Parthian Iran
910.description: The Hellenistic Seleucid period, the rise of the Arsacid Parthian Empire as a rival to Rome, the Silk Road trade, and the synthesis of Iranian and Hellenistic cultures.

sub_clusters.name: Seleucid Hellenistic Period
sub_clusters.description: Alexander's conquest and its aftermath, the Seleucid Empire's control of the Iranian plateau, Hellenistic cultural influence, and the gradual Iranian reassertion.

sub_clusters.name: Parthian (Arsacid) Empire
sub_clusters.description: The Arsacid dynasty's creation of the Parthian Empire, its rivalry with Rome, the catastrophic Roman defeat at Carrhae, the Silk Road wealth, and the feudal military system.
key_events: Battle of Carrhae — Parthians destroy Roman army under Crassus (53 BC)
Parthia and Rome fight repeatedly over Armenia and Mesopotamia

920.name: Sassanid Empire
920.description: The Sassanid dynasty's revival of Iranian imperial grandeur, Zoroastrianism as state religion, the rivalry with Rome/Byzantium, and the eventual Arab Muslim conquest.

sub_clusters.name: Sassanid Foundation and Expansion
sub_clusters.description: Ardashir I's overthrow of the Parthians, Shapur I's capture of Roman Emperor Valerian, the codification of Zoroastrianism, and the development of elaborate court culture.
key_events: Shapur I captures Roman Emperor Valerian at the Battle of Edessa (260 AD)
Sassanid rock reliefs at Naqsh-e Rostam celebrate imperial triumphs

sub_clusters.name: Khosrow I and Sassanid Zenith
sub_clusters.description: Khosrow I Anushirvan's golden age of justice and learning, the Academy of Gondishapur, Khosrow II's near-destruction of Byzantium, and the exhausting final Roman-Persian war.

sub_clusters.name: Arab Muslim Conquest of Iran
sub_clusters.description: The Rashidun Caliphate's conquest of the Sassanid Empire, the decisive battles of Qadisiyyah and Nahavand, the death of Yazdegerd III, and the end of Zoroastrian political dominance.
key_events: Battle of al-Qadisiyyah — Arab forces defeat the Sassanid army (636 AD)
Battle of Nahavand — 'Victory of Victories' ends Sassanid resistance (642 AD)

920.name: Islamic Iran and Persian Cultural Renaissance
920.description: Iran's transformation under Islam, the Abbasid revolution with strong Iranian participation, the Samanid, Buyid, and Seljuk dynasties, and the Persian literary and scientific golden age.

sub_clusters.name: Iranian Dynasties and Persian Revival
sub_clusters.description: The Tahirid, Saffarid, and Samanid dynasties that restored Persian language and culture, Ferdowsi's Shahnameh preserving Iran's pre-Islamic heritage, and the rise of New Persian.
key_events: Ferdowsi completes the Shahnameh (Book of Kings), the Persian national epic (1010 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Seljuk Period and Scientific Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: The Great Seljuk Empire's adoption of Persian administrative culture, Nizam al-Mulk's madrasas, Omar Khayyam's calendar and poetry, and Avicenna's medical and philosophical works.
key_events: Omar Khayyam reforms the Persian calendar — more accurate than the Gregorian (1079 AD)

930.name: Mongol, Ilkhanid, and Timurid Iran
930.description: The catastrophic Mongol invasion, Iran under Ilkhanid and Timurid rule, the devastation of cities and population, and the paradoxical flourishing of Persian miniature painting and poetry.

sub_clusters.name: Mongol Invasion and Ilkhanate
sub_clusters.description: Genghis Khan's and Hulagu's devastating invasions destroying cities like Nishapur and Baghdad, the Ilkhanate's adoption of Persian culture, and the conversion to Islam under Ghazan Khan.
key_events: Genghis Khan destroys Nishapur, Merv, and other major Iranian cities (1220–1221)
Hulagu sacks Baghdad, ending the Abbasid Caliphate (1258)

sub_clusters.name: Timurid Iran and Cultural Flourishing
sub_clusters.description: Timur's devastating campaigns followed by the Timurid Renaissance under Shah Rukh and Sultan Husayn Bayqara, the Herat school of miniature painting, and the poetry of Jami.

930.name: Safavid Empire
930.description: The Safavid dynasty's unification of Iran, the imposition of Twelver Shia Islam as the state religion, Isfahan's architectural splendor, and the creation of modern Iranian national identity.

sub_clusters.name: Shah Ismail and Shia Conversion
sub_clusters.description: Shah Ismail I's founding of the Safavid Empire, the forced conversion of Iran from Sunni to Twelver Shia Islam, and the fateful Battle of Chaldiran against the Ottomans.
key_events: Shah Ismail I conquers Tabriz and declares Twelver Shiism the state religion (1501)
Battle of Chaldiran — Ottoman victory establishes the Safavid-Ottoman frontier (1514)

sub_clusters.name: Shah Abbas the Great
sub_clusters.description: Shah Abbas I's transformation of Isfahan into one of the world's most magnificent cities, military reforms with the ghulam system, defeat of the Uzbeks and Ottomans, and commercial diplomacy with Europe.
key_events: Shah Abbas I moves the capital to Isfahan and builds Naqsh-e Jahan Square (1598)
Safavid forces recapture Baghdad from the Ottomans (1623)

sub_clusters.name: Safavid Decline and Fall
sub_clusters.description: The weakening of Safavid power, the Afghan invasion and sack of Isfahan, the brief Afsharid restoration under Nadir Shah, and the disintegration of central authority.

940.name: Afsharid, Zand, and Qajar Iran
940.description: Nadir Shah's brief imperial brilliance, the Zand interlude, and the long Qajar dynasty marked by territorial losses to Russia and Britain, the tobacco protest, and the Constitutional Revolution.

sub_clusters.name: Nadir Shah and Zand Dynasty
sub_clusters.description: Nadir Shah's military conquests including the sack of Delhi, the short-lived Afsharid dynasty, and Karim Khan Zand's relatively peaceful and prosperous rule from Shiraz.
key_events: Nadir Shah sacks Delhi and seizes the Peacock Throne and Koh-i-Noor diamond (1739)

sub_clusters.name: Qajar Dynasty and the Great Game
sub_clusters.description: The Qajar dynasty's loss of the Caucasus to Russia, the Great Game rivalry between Britain and Russia in Iran, the Tobacco Protest of 1891, and the Constitutional Revolution of 1905–1906.
key_events: Treaties of Gulistan (1813) and Turkmenchay (1828) cede the Caucasus to Russia
Tobacco Protest — first successful mass movement against foreign concessions (1891)
Constitutional Revolution establishes Iran's first parliament (Majles) (1906)

950.name: Pahlavi Dynasty and Modernization
950.description: Reza Shah's authoritarian modernization, the Allied occupation in WWII, Mossadegh and the oil nationalization crisis, the Shah's White Revolution, and the growing opposition leading to revolution.

sub_clusters.name: Reza Shah Modernization
sub_clusters.description: Reza Khan's coup, the founding of the Pahlavi dynasty, forced modernization including unveiling, the Trans-Iranian Railway, and the Allied invasion forcing his abdication.
key_events: Reza Khan deposes the Qajars and founds the Pahlavi dynasty (1925)
Iran renamed from Persia by government decree (1935)

sub_clusters.name: Mossadegh and Oil Nationalization
sub_clusters.description: Mohammad Reza Shah's early reign, Prime Minister Mossadegh's nationalization of Iranian oil, the CIA/MI6-orchestrated coup (Operation Ajax), and its lasting impact on Iranian politics.
key_events: Mossadegh nationalizes Iran's oil industry (1951)
CIA-MI6 coup d'état overthrows Mossadegh and restores the Shah's power (1953)

sub_clusters.name: White Revolution and Opposition
sub_clusters.description: The Shah's White Revolution reforms, rapid Westernization, SAVAK repression, Ayatollah Khomeini's exile and growing clerical opposition, and the revolutionary movement.

950.name: Islamic Revolution and Iran-Iraq War
950.description: The 1979 Islamic Revolution establishing the world's first Shia theocratic republic, the hostage crisis, and the devastating eight-year war with Iraq.

sub_clusters.name: 1979 Islamic Revolution
sub_clusters.description: The mass revolution overthrowing the Shah, Ayatollah Khomeini's return from exile, the establishment of the Islamic Republic, and the US Embassy hostage crisis.
key_events: Shah flees Iran; Ayatollah Khomeini returns from exile (January–February 1979)
Iranian students seize the US Embassy — 444-day hostage crisis begins (November 1979)

sub_clusters.name: Iran-Iraq War
sub_clusters.description: Saddam Hussein's invasion of Iran, eight years of devastating trench warfare, chemical weapons use, the 'war of the cities,' and the ceasefire with over one million casualties.
key_events: Iraq invades Iran, beginning the longest conventional war of the 20th century (1980)
UN-brokered ceasefire ends the war; Khomeini calls it 'drinking poison' (1988)

960.name: Post-War Islamic Republic and Nuclear Crisis
960.description: Iran's post-Khomeini evolution: Rafsanjani's reconstruction, Khatami's reform movement, Ahmadinejad's confrontation, the nuclear deal and its collapse, and Iran's regional influence.

sub_clusters.name: Reconstruction and Reform Era
sub_clusters.description: Rafsanjani's post-war economic reconstruction, President Khatami's reform movement and 'Dialogue of Civilizations,' the student protests of 1999, and the conservative backlash.

sub_clusters.name: Nuclear Crisis and Sanctions
sub_clusters.description: The exposure of Iran's nuclear program, Ahmadinejad's confrontational presidency, the Green Movement of 2009, crippling international sanctions, and the JCPOA nuclear agreement.
key_events: Green Movement protests erupt after disputed presidential election (2009)
JCPOA nuclear agreement signed between Iran and P5+1 (2015)

sub_clusters.name: US Withdrawal from JCPOA and Regional Influence
sub_clusters.description: Trump's withdrawal from the JCPOA, 'maximum pressure' sanctions, the assassination of General Soleimani, the Mahsa Amini protests, and Iran's 'Axis of Resistance' across the Middle East.
key_events: US assassinates IRGC General Qasem Soleimani in Baghdad (January 2020)
Mahsa Amini protests — 'Woman, Life, Freedom' movement sweeps Iran (September 2022)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
